themes_detail.label: Street Lights Going Dark
themes_detail.summary: Street light outages spiked to 38 complaints THIS WEEK versus a baseline average of 12.4 per week (207% increase, z-score 8.8), suggesting a sudden widespread infrastructure failure affecting public safety and visibility across Far Rockaway.
evidence: 38 street light complaints THIS WEEK vs. 12.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (207% spike, z-score: 8.8)
Spike is statistically significant and represents acute infrastructure degradation
Aligns with broader infrastructure concerns evident in recurring DEP capital budget requests for street/sewer improvements
reporting_angles: Interview DOE/DEP about root cause: equipment failure, storm damage, maintenance backlog, or budget constraints?
Map outages to identify if concentrated in specific neighborhoods (Edgemere, Arverne, mainland Far Rockaway)
Safety angle: how long are repairs taking, what are safety risks for pedestrians and cyclists?

themes_detail.label: Commercial Noise Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Commercial noise complaints surged to 12 THIS WEEK, a 210% spike over the 8-week baseline of 3.9 per week (z-score 5.59), suggesting a new or intensified commercial activity disturbance affecting residential quality of life.
evidence: 12 commercial noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 3.9 weekly average (210% increase, z-score: 5.59)
Contrasts with residential noise DOWN 27% this week, isolating commercial sector as the driver
Street/sidewalk noise also UP 162% (34 complaints vs. 13.0 avg), suggesting outdoor commercial activity
reporting_angles: Identify what commercial operations triggered complaints: construction, bar/restaurant hours, delivery trucks, equipment?
Link to active ULURP/development projects (Edgemere Commons Phase 2B, 14-10 Beach Channel Drive rezoning) — are new businesses opening or construction ramping up?
Interview affected residents about timing and specific sources of noise

themes_detail.label: Water Quality Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Water quality complaints exploded to 4 TWO WEEKS AGO from a baseline of 0.1 per week (3100% increase, z-score 11.72, highest severity flagged), indicating a potential contamination event or system failure affecting drinking water safety in the district.
evidence: 4 water quality complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly average (3100% spike, z-score: 11.72, highest severity)
Spike is now 1-2 weeks old; critical to determine if issue is resolved or ongoing
Fits pattern of repeated DEP capital budget requests for sewer development and water system improvements (unsolved infrastructure need)
reporting_angles: URGENT: Contact DEP for incident reports — was there a contamination event, boil water advisory, or system break 2+ weeks ago?
Obtain water quality test data from DEP for Far Rockaway distribution zones around time of spike
Interview residents who filed complaints about taste, color, odor, or health symptoms
Context: does this connect to the 'Rockaway Whale' article (environmental warning)? Are dead fish/marine life linked to water quality?

themes_detail.label: Street Signs Damaged
themes_detail.summary: Damaged street sign complaints jumped to 21 LAST WEEK from a baseline of 3.1 per week (572% increase, z-score 11.07), suggesting either storm damage or accelerating neglect of street-level infrastructure.
evidence: 21 damaged street sign complaints LAST WEEK vs. 3.1 weekly average (572% spike, z-score: 11.07)
High statistical significance suggests concentrated incident rather than gradual deterioration
May indicate weather event (recent storm) or systematic maintenance failure
reporting_angles: Was there recent severe weather (wind, water damage) that caused widespread sign damage?
Check DOT repair backlogs for Far Rockaway — how long do repairs take?
Walk streets to document current condition and photograph damaged signs for visual story

themes_detail.label: Dead Trees and Environmental Decline
themes_detail.summary: Dead or dying tree complaints spiked to 3 THIS WEEK from a baseline of 0.4 per week (700% increase, z-score 5.42), potentially signaling environmental stress, salt damage, or deferred maintenance in a district repeatedly requesting park reconstruction funding.
evidence: 3 dead/dying tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average (700% spike, z-score: 5.42)
Community board has repeated budget requests for park reconstruction and new amenities, suggesting deferred environmental maintenance
Aligns with broader environmental concern in district (reflected in 'Rockaway Whale' opinion piece about environmental risk)
reporting_angles: Interview Parks Dept about tree health assessment — are trees dying from salt spray, soil contamination, or lack of maintenance?
Map dead trees to specific parks/locations to identify environmental hotspots
Connect to larger climate resilience and waterfront environmental concerns in the Rockaways
